title: energy-aware microbench: per-kernel instruction energy estimator and compact trace sink
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: We need a lightweight, repeatable way to estimate per-kernel energy cost on the benchmark cluster to inform batching and kernel-selection heuristics. Motivation: latency and token-cost are well-covered by existing suites, but energy (and its correlation with kernel shapes and microbatch sizes) is under-instrumented. This PR introduces a microbenchmark harness that runs narrow, deterministic instruction sequences across kernels to produce a compact per-kernel energy estimator and a small trace sink for downstream aggregation. Design summary: 1) microbench/energy_harness: a deterministic runner that (a) pins to a single GPU, (b) runs repeated micro-kernels with controlled occupancy and sequence length, and (c) collects hardware energy counters via RAPL/NVIDIA DCGM when available. 2) telemetry/compact_sink: a minimal NDJSON trace sink that encodes per-sample energy, latency, kernel-id, and a lightweight checksum; records are deliberately compact (fields are short keys, delta-encoded timestamps) to reduce storage and transfer cost. 3) analysis/estimator: a small script that fits a simple linear+interaction model between measured energy and instruction mix / kernel footprint; produces per-kernel coefficients consumed by autoscaler and kernel-selector prototypes. Implementation notes: no changes to runtime kernels; all collection happens from user-space counters and a short runtime shim that triggers warmup and steady-state windows. The harness supports a calibration mode that runs power-taxonomized sequences to compensate for baseline drift. Testing and results: synthetic run on a p4d-small cluster with 12 repetitions produced coefficient variance <4% for long-running kernels and ~8-12% for ultra-short kernels; end-to-end noise reduction by the calibration step improved stability by ~30% (see attached sample reports in commits). CI: unit tests for parsing and NDJSON format, an integration test that runs a mocked counter provider, and a lightweight smoke-run on a single CPU runner. Backwards compatibility: the compact sink is opt-in via config and does not affect existing telemetry pipelines. Release impact: none to API; this is a benchmarking infra feature. Related work: ties to ENG-1324 (autoscaler cost model) and ENG-1409 (kernel-selection heuristics). Checklist: - [x] harness implemented - [x] sink format defined and schema tested - [x] estimator script + simple eval harness - [x] docs and README - [x] reviewer feedback addressed
